tasks.analysis: One of the topics psychologists investigate is our capacity to understand the mental states of others. This ability is fundamental for social interaction because it enables us to predict and explain the behavior of others. Is this skill innate or shaped by experience? Is understanding others’ mental states a matter of simulation (imagining ourselves in their place) or theory (applying a set of rules or concepts)?
